title: Japanese for Restaurants in 9 Comic Scenes | Guess, Listen, Say It (Travel Japanese)
lead: Everything you need to say in a Japanese restaurant, from the door to the bill, in nine comic scenes. Guess first, then listen twice and say it.

intro.title:
Japan restaurant
**9 phrases**
intro.say: Nine scenes in a Japanese restaurant. Guess each line before the answer.

phrases.scene: At the entrance under a plain dark-blue fabric door curtain, Jiwoo raises one hand slightly and calls toward the waitress inside; Minjun stands behind her.
phrases.label: Calling the staff
phrases.when: To call a server over, say this.
phrases.tip: Raise your hand a little as you say it. It also means sorry, so you will use it everywhere.
phrases.short: Call a server in a Japanese restaurant

phrases.scene: Just inside the door, the waitress asks a question with a polite gesture; Jiwoo answers holding up two fingers, Minjun next to her nods.
phrases.label: How many people
phrases.when: At the door, the server asks how many people. For two, answer like this.
phrases.tip: The server asks: nanmei-sama desu ka. Alone, say hitori desu. Three people, sannin desu. Showing fingers works too.
phrases.hear: 何名様ですか？ (Nanmei-sama desu ka?) = How many people?

phrases.ja: 英語のメニューはありますか？
phrases.scene: Seated at a wooden table, Jiwoo holds an open menu covered in illegible squiggles and looks puzzled, asking the waitress standing beside the table.
phrases.label: English menu
phrases.pron: Eigo no menyuu wa arimasu ka?
phrases.ko: Do you have an English menu?
phrases.when: If the menu is only in Japanese, ask this.
phrases.tip: Many restaurants in tourist areas have an English menu. If there are only photos, the next phrase is all you need.

phrases.scene: Jiwoo points at a photo of a bowl of food on the open menu, smiling at the waitress who holds a small order pad.
phrases.label: I'll have this
phrases.when: Point at the menu and say this.
phrases.tip: For two, say kore o futatsu kudasai. With this one phrase you can order almost anything.
phrases.short: Order anything in Japan with one phrase

phrases.scene: Jiwoo looks up curiously at the waitress, who smiles and gestures with an open hand toward a wall of food photos.
phrases.label: Recommendation
phrases.when: Not sure what to eat? Ask for a recommendation.
phrases.tip: When the server points at a dish, just say kore o kudasai.

phrases.ja: わさび抜きでお願いします。
phrases.scene: Sushi set on the table; Jiwoo makes a gentle 'no thanks' gesture with both hands at a tiny green dab of wasabi on a plate, Minjun laughs.
phrases.label: Without wasabi
phrases.when: At a sushi place, if you don't want wasabi, say this.
phrases.tip: Nuki means without. Swap in other things too: green onion is negi, so negi-nuki de onegai shimasu.

phrases.scene: After the meal, empty bowls on the table; Jiwoo raises her hand politely toward the waitress across the room.
phrases.label: The bill
phrases.when: When you have finished eating, ask for the bill like this.
phrases.tip: In many restaurants in Japan you pay at the counter, not at the table. There is no tipping.

phrases.scene: At a small cash register counter, Jiwoo holds up a credit card and asks the waitress behind the counter.
phrases.label: Paying by card
phrases.when: If you want to pay by card, ask first.
phrases.tip: Some small restaurants and ramen shops still take cash only, so carry a little cash.

bonus.scene: Leaving through the fabric door curtain, Jiwoo and Minjun bow slightly and smile; the waitress bows back warmly.
bonus.label: When you leave
bonus.when: Finally, say this on your way out. The staff will really appreciate it.

outro.title: Recap: **9 phrases**
outro.say: All the phrases are in the description. Tell us in the comments how many you got right. Next: the convenience store. Subscribe so you don't miss it.
